Act Date of commencement of : 20.07.2023 recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 14.11.2024 was pronounced Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s  02 03 28  JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 16.12.2021.
2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 16.12.2021 at about 9.00 a.m., petitioner has parked the car bearing Reg. No. KA-05- MD-9762 on Bangalore-Kolar road, near Gottipura Gate, on extreme left side of the road by following traffic rules, at that time a Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-08-M-8043 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's car from behind. Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained multiple head injuries and also car completely damaged. 
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, Hoskote for first aid treatment and admitted as in-patient and thereafter shifted to Apollo Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance, food, transport and other charges and petitioner has future medical expenses also.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 52 years, the petitioner was a Contractor. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do job and hence lost his earnings. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Petitioner further stated that,
due to the impact of accident, his car was completely damaged and he has spent Rs.3,40,000/-
towards repair of his car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MD- 9762. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.

2 3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, hence placed exparte. 
The respondent No.2 filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. This respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liabilities if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 134(c), 158(6) and 170 of M. V. Act. This respondent further submits that, the alleged accident took place on 16.12.2021, however the complaint is lodged on 17.12.2021 i.e., after lapse of 1 day from the date of alleged accident. This respondent specifically submits that, the offending car was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle. No valid reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint. Further, this respondent submits that, at the time of alleged accident the driver was not holding Driving License to drive the vehicle. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons,
it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 16.12.2021 at about 9.00 a.m., while petitioner was parked the car bearing Reg.
No. KA-05-MD-9762 on Bangalore-Kolar Road, near Gottipura Gate, on extreme left side of the road by following traffic rules, at that time, Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg.
No. KA-08-M-8043 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner's Car from behind and caused the accident and due to tremendous impact the petitioner sustained multiple head injuries and also Car completely damaged as alleged by him?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom? 
3. What order or Award? 
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, she has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.20, examined one Anthony Maria as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.21 to 23, examined Dr. Shailesh A. V Rao as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.24 to 26 and also examined Shams Tabraj as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.27 to 29 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents. 
6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative. 
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place she met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition. He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 20. Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.6 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P7 is the Statement before police, Ex.P8 is the Notarized copy of RC, Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12 are the Income Tax returns, Ex.P.13 is the Discharge summary, 
Ex.P.14 is the vehicle damage estimation bill, Ex.P.15 is the photos with CD, Ex.P.16 is the payment receipt, Ex.P.17 is the medical bills, Ex.P.18 is the certificate u/s 65(B) of Indian Evidence Act,
Ex.P19 is the Notarized copy of Driving License, Ex.P.20 is the Notarized copy of Driving License. 
10. On 16.12.2021 at about 9.00 a.m., petitioner has parked the car bearing Reg. No.
KA-05-MD-9762 on Bangalore-Kolar road, near Gottipura Gate, on extreme left side of the road by following traffic rules, at that time a Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-08-M-8043 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's car from behind. Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained multiple head injuries and also car completely damaged. 
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, Hoskote for first aid treatment and admitted as in-patient and thereafter shifted to Apollo Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as inpatient. Accordingly, the Hoskote Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.400/2021. After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC. Further, petitioner also sought Rs.3,40,000/- towards the repair of his Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MD-9762.
11. The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person. It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others. In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act. 
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something. In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 08-M-8043.
12. As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ". 
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Hoskote Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2. On receiving the First Vinayaka Naidu vs S. Sankesh on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72579010/
4 Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 400/2021. The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14. During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P.1 to 7 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of the driver of offending Car. The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.6, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending Car U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC. 
The Ex.P.5 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question. Further in this case, contesting respondent has taken contention that, the Car bearing Reg. NO. KA-08-M-8043 was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle and the said alleged accident is caused due to the sole negligence of petitioner. Further during cross- examination of petitioner i.e., PW.1 learned counsel for respondent No.2 suggested that, alleged accident is not caused due to the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-08-M- 8043 and petitioner himself parked his car in the middle of the road, as such accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner only, but witness denied the said suggestion. Moreover, in order to prove his contention contesting respondent failed to adduce evidence before this court. Hence, as per the decision reported in (1999) 3 SCC 573 between Vidhyadhar vs Manikrao & Anr.
presumption would arise that the case set up by the respondent is not correct. 
15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place. By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-08-M-8043. Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative. 
17. ISSUE No.2: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Silicon City Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter she was shifted to Apollo Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment. Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
18. PAIN AND SUFFERING: In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, wherein he treated as an inpatient from 16.12.2021 to 17.12.2021 and thereafter shifted to Apollo Hospital for further treatment, wherein he treated as an inpatient from 17.12.2021 to 21.12.2021. The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.13 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Silicon City Hospital,
Vinayaka Naidu vs S. Sankesh on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72579010/
5 Bangalore for 01 day and thereafter took treatment at Apollo Hospital, Bangalore for 05 days. He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.3, which disclose that petitioner sustained left frontal subdural hematoma, right parietal parenchymal hematoma, right basi frontal hypo density and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature. Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience. Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and suffering. 
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES: The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 39 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.17 to the tune of Rs.2,79,647/-. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,79,647/-
towards medical expenses. 
20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD: The petitioner has produced Ex.P.13 Discharge summaries issued by Silicon City Hospital and Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru, it reveals that,
the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 16.12.2021 to 17.12.2021 and 17.12.2021 to 21.12.2021 i.e. for total 06 days. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was a contractor and earning a sum of Rs.60,000/- per month. But respondent No.2 disputed the income of petitioner. In order to prove his income petitioner relied upon the Income Tax return for the year 2018-2019, 2019-2020,
2020-2021 and 2021-2022 i.e., Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12. As per Ex.P.9 i.e., Income Tax return for the year 2018-2019, gross total income of the petitioner is Rs.5,47,647/-. As per Ex.P.10 Income Tax return for the year 2019-2020 , gross total income of the petitioner is Rs.5,55,200/-. As per Ex.P.11 Income Tax return for the year 2020- 2021, gross total income of the petitioner is Rs.4,95,200/-. As per Ex.P.12 Income Tax return for the year 2021-2022, gross total income of the petitioner is Rs.4,96,500/-. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that, petitioner has not produced any document in order to show the exact income of the petitioner. As such, income tax returns produced at Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.12 cannot be considered as proof of income of petitioner. The tax returns submitted by the petitioner are issued by the Income Tax department. As such, there is no impediment to consider the said documents as evidence to assess the income of the petitioner. In this case, accident is caused on 16.12.2021. Ex. P.9 to Ex .P.12 i.e., tax assessment return are submitted much before the accident. Hence, it would be appropriate to consider the annual income of the petitioner is Rs. 4,95,200/-. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.41,266/-
p.m. as per above decision. Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.82,532/- under this head. 
21. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Sailesh A. V. Rao in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 who has opined that, total disability of whole body disability at 20%. 
Admittedly, the PW.3 is not a treated doctor. Same was admitted by the PW.3 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.3 reads as follows :
"It is true to say that, I have not treated the petitioner."

6 He was sworn that, petitioner sustained left frontal subdural hematoma, right parietal parenchymal hematoma, right basi frontal hypo density and further depose that, petitioner has got 20% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. The said PW.3 doctor is qualified neuro- sergeon and has deposed that petitioner has sustained whole body disability at 20%. The respondent No.2 who has cross-examined the petitioner did not establish as to how the disability was lesser than 20% as assessed by PW.2. Hence, this tribunal came to conclusion that there is 15%
of disability to the petitioner. PW.3 is only record keeper who has only produced the medical documents and his evidence is formal in nature. 
22. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined. 
Ex.P.19 is the Driving License of the petitioner, wherein his D.O.B is mentioned as 28.06.1969 and accident took place in the year 2022. Accordingly, I assess his age as 52 years at the time of this accident. As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '11'. Hence Rs.41,266 X 12 X 11 X 15% = Rs.8,17,066/-. Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.8,17,066/-. 
23. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES: 
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Silicon City Hospital, Bengaluru and again to Apollo Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 16.12.2021 to 17.12.2021 and 17.12.2021 to 21.12.2021 i.e. for total 06 days. 
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges. 
24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: The petitioner was aged about 52 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works. He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. 
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness. 
25. VEHICLE DAMAGE EXPENSES: In this case, petitioner contended that, he is the owner of vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-05- MD-9762. After the accident shifted his car to Hoskote police station for IMV Inspection. The RTO inspected his vehicle and mentioned the damages caused to his vehicle in IMV Report. Further he contended that, his car front bumper, Radiator, Radiator grill,
condenser, front both sides head light assembly, wheel fender damaged, rear bumper, dicky door,
number plate and rear chassis damaged, rear windscreen glass broken, rear both sides brake light units, indicators and quarter panels damaged. 
In support of his contention he relied upon the Ex.P.5 as well as Final report at Ex.P.6. In final report it reveals that, offending vehicle as well vehicle of the petitioner are damaged and same is also seen from Ex.P.15 Photos of petitioner vehicle, wherein it clearly reveals that his vehicle is damaged Vinayaka Naidu vs S. Sankesh on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72579010/
7 heavily. Further in Ex.P.5 IMV Report RTO has mentioned the following damages :
a. Front bumper, number plate, radiator, radiator grill, condenser, number plate and engile bonnet damaged. 
b. Front both side headlight assembly and wheel fender damaged. 
c. Rear bumper, Dicky door, number plate & rear chassis damaged. 
d. Rear windscreen glass broken. 
e. Rear both side brake light units, indicators & quarter panels damaged. 
f. Rear right side door was damaged. 
g. Rear right side suspension system damaged. During the course of cross-examination, though the advocate for insurance company not denied the damages caused to the vehicle of the petitioner, but he has taken defence that he is claiming more amount then the actual amount spent towards the repair of said car. 
The learned counsel for insurance company also suggested that, petitioner is claiming OD claim towards the car repair, but in order to show the said fact he has not furnished any records. Further, petitioner in order to show the amount spent towards the repair of the said damaged car he has furnished the estimation report at Ex.P.14 and also final bill paid towards the amount paid by him to the owner of the Link Motors. In support of the said contention he also examined the owner of the Link Motors as PW.4, in his examination he deposed about the damages caused to the vehicle of the petitioner as well as repair done by him and also received the amount of Rs.3,33,320/- towards the payment. As stated above respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence in order to disprove the claim made by the petitioner in respect of damages caused to the petitioner's vehicle as well as motor vehicle report issued by the RTO. In such circumstances there is no materials on record to disbelieve the evidence of petitioner inrespect of amount spent towards the repair of his car. So, all these facts clearly goes to show that, petitioner has spent Rs.3,33,320/- towards repair of the said car. Hence, Rs.3,33,320/- is awarded under the head of vehicle damage expenses. 
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 2,79,647/- 3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 82,532/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning, Rs. 8,17,066/-

8 Disability 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
loss of happiness. 
7 Vehicle damage expenses Rs. 3,33,320/-
Total Rs. 16,02,565/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,02,565/- under various heads. 
26. LIABILITY: As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-08-M-8043 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending Car. The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle. Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner. 
27. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative. 
28. ISSUE No.3: In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.16,02,565/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest. The respondent No.2 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 08-M-8043.

summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained multiple head injuries and also car completely damaged.
After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.

Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending Maruthi Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 08-M-8043.
